answer: Because the kernel deposit is held in the quartz escrow, the dawn audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge burns a deposit of 51 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases thus burns capital on every one it does not finish. A farm of 92 pays that 98 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
